text:
maria: Quick heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selection rollout (auto-swap) I observed a host CPU spike on the preparse/ingress path for streaming requests. p50 CPU ~2-3x. Tokenization time is up and KV cache miss rate increased ~4%. Anyone else seeing this? /cc @lee @dinesh :eyes:
dinesh: saw a short spike in prod around 02:12 UTC. Traces indicate a drop in batch sizes — batching heuristic fell back to conservative path when seq_len distribution shifted.
lee: I pulled a trace. grpc frames look fragmented — many tiny writev syscalls. syscall count up, copy overhead visible. My guess: kernel selection change increased per-token decode cost and exposed writev fragmentation.
jess: I reproduced locally with a replay; it's short-lived but consistent. Posted a quick flamegraph + pprof snippet below.
jess: ```
pprof top (cpu):
  35%  runtime::tokenize
  20%  net::writev
  15%  preparse::parse_frame
  10%  kvcache::lookup
   5%  kernel_select::score
```
maria: Huh — kv misses higher which could explain more kernel work. Why are misses up? eviction policy? fragment reordering?
andrew: I can repro with the harness. When batch size drops <4 we see per-request coldstarts in the KV cache. Heuristics currently bias very small batches for latency which increases async cache churn.
infra-bot: deploy redwood/ingress/kernsel-rollout succeeded (canary 100%)
sre-bot: alert: host-cpu > 80% on role=ingress for 12m (autothrottle applied)
dinesh: Proposed quick mitigations: 1) add guard to batching heuristic to prefer bumping min batch to 4 in streaming mode when kv hit-rate is low, 2) coalesce small writev calls on proxy side to reduce syscall overhead.
lee: I prototyped a tiny proxy shim that coalesces writev calls: `proxy::outbuf.coalesce()` — syscall count dropped ~40% in my local run.
jess: Suggest canary plan: deploy coalesce shim + batching guard to 5% of ingress. Monitor p50 latency, cpu, kv-miss-rate, syscall_count, and model quality.
maria: +1. I'll open a short PR for the batching guard and add an eval set to detect regressions. :shipit:
andrew: Plan summary I will run tonight: 1) canary coalesce shim (5%) 2) bump streaming min-batch to 4 in heuristic 3) collect pprof + kv hit-rate + syscall metrics 4) rollback if quality drop > 0.5 BLEU or token loss on evals.
maria: Thanks — please post canary metrics in #eng-runtime and ping if any red flags.
